title: PPLLaVA: Varied Video Sequence Understanding With Prompt Guidance
claim: Each question needs only a small part of a long input, so prompt-guided compression keeps accuracy with far fewer tokens.
layout: 2 panels, left example and right plot, with red keywords and green delta arrows
description: Panel (a), on the left, shows two filmstrip rows of animated video frames: a closed eye, an EMOTIONS title card, a winged figure, a butterfly, a red crystal, a girl, a mirror scene and a closing card. Below the strips are three user questions in speech bubbles, each with its key phrase in red: the girl's feelings, the butterfly count, and three-dimensional graphics. Hollow arrows link each question to the one or two frames that answer it, drawn from a stacked deck of frames. This shows that each question depends on only a small part of the video. Panel (b), on the right, is a line plot of VideoMME accuracy against the number of visual tokens. The red PPLLaVA curve sits above the blue LLaVA-Video curve at every budget. Dashed green arrows mark gains of +6.86 and +4.40 at 1000 and 2000 tokens.
caption: (a) An instance from VideoMME [ref]. The crucial information pertains to only a small portion of the video for different questions. (b) Performance comparison of PPLLaVA-LLaVA-Video with LLaVA-Video baseline on VideoMME-Overall (wo subtitles), which shows the number of visual tokens input to the LLM and the corresponding model performance.
abstract: In the past year, video-based large language models (Video LLMs) have achieved impressive progress, particularly in their ability to process long videos through extremely extended context lengths. However, this comes at the cost of significantly increased computational overhead due to the massive number of visual tokens, making efficiency a major bottleneck. In this paper, we identify the root of this inefficiency as the high redundancy in video content. To address this, we propose a novel pooling strategy that enables aggressive token compression while retaining instruction-relevant visual semantics. Our model, Prompt-guided Pooling LLaVA (PPLLaVA), introduces three key components: a CLIP-based visual-prompt alignment module that identifies regions of interest based on user instructions, a prompt-guided pooling mechanism that adaptively compresses the visual sequence using convolution-style pooling, and a clip context extension module tailored for processing long and complex prompts in visual dialogues. With up to 18x token reduction, PPLLaVA maintains strong performance across tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on diverse video understanding benchmarks-ranging from image-to-video tasks such as captioning and QA to long-form video reasoning-while significantly improving inference throughput. Codes have been available at https://github.com/farewellthree/PPLLaVA.
